question: Ram went to a shop and observed that the list price of a fan is ₹ 3,600. If the retailer has bought the fan for ₹ 2,800, then find the trade discount (correct to one decimal place).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Trade Discount = List Price − Buying Price

Discount = 3600 − 2800 = 800

Discount % = (Discount ÷ List Price) × 100

Discount % = (800 ÷ 3600) × 100 = 200 ÷ 9 ≈ 22.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

List Price (MP) of the fan = ₹ 3,600

Buying Price (SP) of the fan = ₹ 2,800

**Formula Used:**

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 
• 
 
 
 MP
 ₹ 3600
 
 
 SP
 ₹ 2800

 

 Discount = ₹ 800

 Discount % = (800 ÷ 3600) × 100 = 22.2%

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 3600 − 2800 = ₹ 800

⇒ Discount % = (800 ÷ 3600) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 80000 ÷ 3600

⇒ Discount % = 200 ÷ 9

⇒ Discount % = 22.222... %

⇒ Correct to one decimal place, Discount % ≈ 22.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price on the label of an article is known as the marked price. Discount is always calculated on the marked price.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, then the single equivalent discount = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Selling Price (SP) Formula

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.
